title: Karachi's World Culture Festival is back
credits: Photos: Shujaat Muzaffar, Muhammad Amir, Muneeb S, pavan gupta, Yvette de Wit / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Karachi is about to welcome artists from all over the world.
The third World Culture Festival runs from the twenty-ninth of October to the twenty-second of November.
That is twenty-five days of theatre, music, dance, film and folk arts.
Artists and cultural representatives from about one hundred and fifty countries are expected.
The festival has grown fast: the first edition had forty-three countries, and the second had one hundred and forty-four.
More than a thousand international artists will perform, alongside over five hundred Pakistani performers.
They come from Sindh, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, Kashmir and the Seraiki region.
There will be a special focus on Sindhi heritage, with traditional instruments like the algoza and the borindo, and a Shah Latif voices festival.
The area around the Arts Council, towards Burns Road, is being turned into an art village, with new lighting and seating.
And about eighty percent of the programmes will be free, with advance registration.
Sindh's culture minister says foreign tourist numbers in the province have risen by about fifty percent in three years.
